issues.problem: The artifact-only guard can be spoofed. The `own` regex accepts any entry whose name merely ends with an artifact suffix, such as `.+\.diff`, `.+\.sha256` or `\..+\.(changed|untracked)`. It also accepts any entry type, including directories and symlinks. So a populated user dir inside the tree still passes as 'inside' and gets the C3-M1 treatment: chmod 700, a self-hiding `*` .gitignore, and its untracked contents left out of the tar by the self-exclusion filter, with rc 0 and no warning. This was reproduced in scratch c4r/run2.sh against --dir=<tree>/d. p9: a user patch d/fix.diff (a realistic `patches/` dir) gives rc 0, mode 755->700, a `*` .gitignore, a tar of only new.txt, and fix.diff gone from git status. p10: release.sha256 behaves the same. p11: a subdir d/work.diff/ holding a.md is accepted, and a.md is hidden and left out of the tar, which breaks the 'any subdirectory -> exit 2' rule. p12: a hidden d/.secret.untracked behaves the same. p13: a symlink link.diff is accepted. Nothing is deleted, but the user files vanish from git status and from every later checkpoint and `team commit`. That is the same consequence class as C3-M1.
issues.fix: In the python classifier, treat an entry as an artifact only when (a) it is a regular file (`os.path.isfile(p) and not os.path.islink(p)`), and (b) its name has the shape this script writes. Anchor the name to the cid timestamp: `^(\.gitignore|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{6}-.+(\.diff|-manifest\.json|-untracked\.tar\.gz|\.sha256)|\.\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{6}-.+\.(changed|untracked))$`. Add one bats test: an existing in-tree dir holding an untracked `fix.diff`, and a second case with a subdir named `work.diff/`, each exits 2 with no .gitignore, mode kept, and the file still in git status. The existing tests 11 and 12 and p1-p3 stay accepted, because they hold only real artifact names or a .gitignore.

not_raised.decision: Not raised. This differs from the orchestrator brief, which expected exit 2, so the orchestrator should decide.
not_raised.rationale: Scratch p7 (an empty .gitignore) and p8 (a `*.log` .gitignore) are accepted with rc 0. The user's .gitignore is kept unchanged and no user file is hidden or lost. The dir gets chmod 700 and the checkpoint files appear in git status. tests/bats/test_mb_team_checkpoint.bats:120-130 (test 12) pins this acceptance, and cycle 3 recorded it as by design: the script respects the user's .gitignore, and git status shows the files, so nothing is hidden. Changing it to exit 2 would mean reversing test 12 and the default-dir behaviour it covers. That is a design choice, not a defect.
